label: Reserves (import cover)
note: How many months of imports the reserves would cover. The buffer that decides whether a shilling shock has to be met by borrowing. CBK publishes this weekly against a statutory floor of four months; USD 15,088 million on this date, about KSh 1.96 trillion at 129.62, down from USD 15,253 million (6.3 months) a week earlier.

label: Gross domestic debt
note: What the government owes at home, the pool every auction on this site draws from. KSh 7,726.50 billion on this date, up from KSh 7,668.41 billion a week earlier. Treasury bonds are 84.27 percent of outstanding securities and bills 15.73, so most new supply is long-dated.

label: Public debt (total)
note: Everything the government owes, domestic and external together — KSh 13,011.89 billion, provisional, against KSh 12,299.48 billion in December 2025. External debt is USD 43.90 billion of it. Deliberately shown as a level and not as a share of GDP: no nominal GDP figure is held here that could be verified, and the ratio is the number this site refuses to estimate. Compiled by the National Treasury and CBK.
